outputs.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Create a new premium industrial-design CONCEPT board for RoboPlanter 工位搭子.
HIGHEST PRIORITY: the user requires a true ALL-IN-ONE APPLIANCE. The planter body, screen, thermal printer, robot-phone cradle, ambient light and base must form ONE unified enclosure and ONE continuous shared footprint. No detached sidecar, no separate phone stand, no gap dividing two appliances. The phone itself can lift out normally, but its cradle is sculpted into the main body.

Input 1 is a previous style exploration: keep its expressive green pixel sprout, warm ivory tactile finish, sage planter collar, paper-note personality and soft lighting. Its separate phone stand MUST be replaced.
Input 2 is the user's original layout reference: preserve the all-in-one functional concept, but improve visual polish, intentional proportions and restrained friendly character.

New design: a beautifully resolved asymmetrical rounded desktop object. LEFT upper front: a large square charcoal display with a bright winking pixel sprout creature. LEFT lower front: a small thermal paper slot in a front-opening cassette, a short paper note emerging like a tongue, tiny coral pull tab. RIGHT: a narrow angled phone well is carved into a raised shoulder of the SAME ivory chassis, with continuous flowing bodywork linking it to the screen housing, not an add-on dock. One thin frosted WS2812 mint ribbon follows the uninterrupted common base outline below both parts. One continuous sculpted lower plinth, one set of feet. The phone camera is articulated above the phone with its top and sides visibly open, no overhanging shroud. Generic robot-camera phone without brand marks.
Real small green foliage emerges from a removable sage-rim inner pot on the rear/top LEFT, visually reads like this companion's hair; keep leaves naturally compact and away from the phone-camera space. Rear wet compartment behind the left main body, slim tinted water-level window on its exposed left side. Dry front screen and paper cassette are separated from rear water area by a continuous internal wall. These are maintenance divisions inside a single appliance, not separate tabletop units. Do not show water under exposed electronics.
Keep believable volume for the full existing SenseCAP Indicator screen assembly and a small thermal printer/roll; no tiny magically thin printer. Existing robot-phone dimensions are not verified: do not label dimensions.

Palette: warm ivory textured matte shell, charcoal screen, sage green removable planter rim, discreet coral cassette tab, soft mint base lighting, lush natural leaves. Friendly character but high-end consumer product, original resolved industrial design, not a toy and not a generic office receipt printer. No neon rainbow, fake vents everywhere, logos or fake technical claims.
Composition: landscape 3:2 presentation board. A large three-quarter hero view on a warm minimal desk occupies 70%, subtle mug and pencil for context. Two smaller consistent views on the right: FRONT VIEW and REAR VIEW of the SAME all-in-one object. Both must show a single common base and integrated phone well. Rear view shows service hatch and water cartridge flush in the main appliance. Four quiet material swatches below. Soft directional studio/window light, tactile surfacing, finely controlled seams, photorealistic product rendering with generous editorial whitespace.
Exact text only:
Title "工位搭子"
Subtitle "ONE BODY. A LITTLE LIFE."
On paper "我在长，别催。"
Sparse callouts "一体式机身", "内嵌手机仓", "像素表情", "独立前开纸仓", "WS2812 柔光"
Footer "一体机概念 · 尺寸与结构待实测"
No other labels, no measurements, no simulated sensor numbers. Legible Chinese typesetting. This is a concept rendering, not an engineering-ready or certified product.

Use case: product-mockup, industrial design service-layout concept.
Create a companion technical concept board for the EXACT ALL-IN-ONE RoboPlanter design in reference image 1. Preserve its continuous ivory body and common base, its screen/paper placement, its built-in phone bay on the right, integrated frosted mint WS2812 base ribbon, sage top planter collar and narrow blue water window on left/rear. Do NOT return to a separate phone stand or separate tabletop modules.

This is a service CUTAWAY of one appliance, not a kit of unattached products. Landscape 3:2, premium ivory background, dark sage headings, highly polished understandable industrial-design rendering.
LEFT TWO THIRDS: large three-quarter cutaway of the same assembled all-in-one machine, outer casing selectively removed to expose conceptual zones, maintaining the continuous chassis outline and shared base.
- On front LEFT are the screen/logic carrier and thermal printer with a realistically sized visible paper roll. A front paper cassette is pulled slightly forwards along subtle guide lines; paper and electronics stay dry.
- Behind the front display, in the rear-left COLUMN, the planter inner pot sits above a dedicated wet cassette. The wet zone is separated from the front paper/electronics and right phone bay by a thick continuous IVORY WALL. No PCB over an uncovered reservoir. The wall extends from under the plant receiver down to the base.
- Wet cassette contains a closed-top translucent fresh-water reservoir and compact pump placeholder. One BLUE supply hose travels upwards wholly within the wet column and ends as an open nozzle above the soil rim (air gap to the soil), never connects to pot bottom.
- Runoff drops from perforated inner-pot bottom into a shallow catcher, then a DIFFERENT GREY drain hose reaches a small separate grey runoff cup, not the fresh-water tank. All drainage remains in rear wet column. Show separate blue UP arrow and grey DOWN arrow, simple and legible.
- Do not draw water anywhere under the full product base, beneath the paper roll, or in the light channel. Light channel is enclosed/dry at the base perimeter.
- On right, INTEGRATED phone recess remains part of the intact common chassis, holding generic black robot-camera phone. Leave open air above and around camera. Draw a faint dotted clearance envelope, no angles or claimed verified reach.
- Keep visible screws, mounting ribs, gaskets and cable allowance conceptually plausible but do not invent PCBs, pinouts or measured dimensions. Recognisable broad service zones are more important than a crowded fake engineering drawing.

RIGHT THIRD, two detail insets:
Upper: rear wet-column sectional concept, blue upwater and grey runoff distinctly separate, closed reservoir and separate catch cup, solid partition at front boundary. No shared pipe. Label wall.
Lower: front paper-cassette access with real-looking small roll visible, continuous main chassis behind it. A small outline of phone camera free-space envelope can appear alongside.
Sparse precise leader lines, only SIX numbered component labels, not more:
"01 可取内盆"
"02 后置湿舱"
"03 连续隔板"
"04 前开纸仓"
"05 内嵌手机仓"
"06 独立灯腔"
Main title "一体外壳，各司其职。"
Subtitle "ONE ENCLOSURE · SERVICE CONCEPT"
Inset headings "上水与余水分开" and "换纸不拆水箱"
Route labels "上水" and "余水"
Footer "结构布局概念 · 非制造图"
Small note "防漏、抗虹吸、散热及相机空间待实测"
No other text, no dimensions, no certifications. The overall geometry must clearly match reference 1 and read as ONE finished device, with only internal maintenance access revealed.
